content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 2024 (Feb–May), especially after sharp declines or spikes.
- Forecast tends to be too flat or slowly rising, failing to capture sudden price rebounds or volatility.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, overshooting downward corrections (e.g., after 80+ peaks, forecast drops too slowly).
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — prices often overshoot lows and fail to return to historical averages.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements, especially in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust quickly when true price deviates from forecast, especially after spikes.
- Overestimates recovery after sharp drops — e.g., after 60–65 price dips, forecast often jumps back to 65+ too soon.
- Underestimates volatility in late 2024 (May) — true prices show sharper swings than model suggests.
- Model fails to capture “rebound after correction” — e.g., after 55–60, forecast stays low while true price rebounds.
